# STM32H743 AIO "Nano" FC + 4-in-1 ESC: Power-Stage, Thermal and DShot Architecture (Job #16)

## 0. Architecture Corrections

Two problems in the brief need fixing before the derivations mean anything.

**1. Firmware partitioning.** ArduPilot runs on the H743 as the flight controller. It does not commutate motors. The 48 kHz PWM is generated by four separate ESC MCUs running AM32 or BLHeli_32-class firmware (e.g., AT32F421 or STM32G071). Two buses link the halves:
- Bidirectional DShot600 (eRPM telemetry) from the H743 to the ESC MCUs.
- Optionally, one UART for KISS-style telemetry back to the H743.

**2. The 80 A burst cannot be sustained on a nano-format board.** Section 4 shows that four channels at 80 A on a 30×30 mm PCB is adiabatic-limited to roughly 2–4 s. The power stage must therefore be spec'd as:
- 80 A per channel, ≤2 s burst, at 6S, with forced airflow, and
- a firmware-enforced I²t limit.

Any "80 A continuous" marketing claim on this form factor is not physically supportable.

**All component values below are design assumptions.** Replace them with datasheet values for the parts actually selected, then re-run the equations.

## 2. Conduction Loss Model

**Commutation.** With 6-step commutation and synchronous (complementary) PWM, two legs carry I_ph at every instant. One HS/LS pair switches, one LS (or HS) is held on, and the third leg floats.

**Path resistance.** Each conducting position (the HS FET or its complementary LS) contributes:

$$R_{eff} = k_T R_{ds,25} + R_{pcb} = 1.5(0.70) + 0.15 = 1.20\ \text{m}\Omega$$

**Per-motor conduction loss.** At any instant, two FET positions are in series with the motor:

$$P_{cond,motor} = 2 I_{ph}^2 R_{eff} = 2(80^2)(1.20\times10^{-3}) = 15.36\ \text{W}$$

This loss is independent of duty, because during off-time the synchronous LS carries the current through the same R_eff.

**Per-FET average.** Each leg is active for 2/3 of the electrical cycle, with current split D : (1−D) between HS and LS:

$$P_{HS} = \tfrac{2}{3} I^2 R_{eff} D,\qquad P_{LS} = \tfrac{2}{3} I^2 R_{eff}(1-D)$$

At burst, D → ~0.95, so the HS FET dominates:

$$P_{HS} \approx \tfrac{2}{3}(6400)(1.2\text{e-}3)(0.95) = 4.86\ \text{W}$$

**4-motor conduction total: 61.4 W.**

---

## 3. Switching Loss Model (48 kHz)

Only one leg PWM-switches at a time, so the per-motor loss equals one HS/LS pair's switching loss.

**(a) V–I overlap, hard-switched HS:**

$$P_{VI} = \tfrac12 V I (t_r+t_f) f_{sw} = \tfrac12(25.2)(80)(40\text{e-}9)(48\text{e}3) = 1.94\ \text{W}$$

**(b) Dead-time body-diode conduction, LS:**

$$P_{dt} = V_{SD} I \cdot 2t_{dt} f_{sw} = 0.8(80)(200\text{e-}9)(48\text{e}3) = 0.61\ \text{W}$$

**(c) Reverse recovery:**

$$P_{rr} = Q_{rr} V f_{sw} = 60\text{e-}9(25.2)(48\text{e}3) = 0.073\ \text{W}$$

**(d) Output capacitance (HS turn-on discharges the LS Coss):**

$$P_{oss} = Q_{oss} V f_{sw} = 0.060\ \text{W}$$

**(e) Gate drive** (dissipated in the driver and R_g, not in the FET):

$$P_g = 2 Q_g V_{gs} f_{sw} = 2(60\text{e-}9)(10)(48\text{e}3) = 0.058\ \text{W}$$

**Per-motor switching loss ≈ 2.74 W.**

**Sensitivity.** P_VI scales linearly with f_sw. Dropping to 24 kHz saves about 1.3 W per motor, at the cost of ripple current and acoustic noise.

## 4. Thermal Model

### 4.1 Totals

| | Per motor | ×4 |
|---|---|---|
| Conduction | 15.36 W | 61.4 W |
| Switching | 2.74 W | 11.0 W |
| Shunt (0.25 mΩ) and copper extras | ~1.6 W | 6.4 W |
| **Total** | **~19.7 W** | **~79 W** |

### 4.2 Hottest-FET junction rise (steady-state bound)

The hottest FET is the PWM-side HS: 4.86 W conduction + 1.94 W overlap + 0.07 W recovery ≈ **6.9 W**.

$$\Delta T_{j-board} = P(R_{\theta jc} + R_{\theta c\text{-}pcb}) = 6.9(0.8 + 2.0) \approx 19\ \text{K}$$

This is acceptable *if* the board stays cool. The board does not stay cool, as 4.3 shows.

### 4.3 Board lumped capacitance (30×30 mm, 1.6 mm, 8 layers × 2 oz)

| Element | Calculation | Heat capacity |
|---|---|---|
| FR-4 | 1.44 cm³ × 1.85 g/cm³ × 1.1 J/gK | 2.9 J/K |
| Copper | 8 × 70 µm × 9 cm² = 0.50 cm³ → 4.5 g × 0.385 J/gK | 1.7 J/K |
| 24 FETs + capacitors | ~3 g | ~1.5 J/K |
| **Total C_th** | | **≈ 6.1 J/K** |

**Convective resistance.** Both faces give 18 cm². With prop wash h ≈ 100 W/m²K:

$$R_{conv} = \frac{1}{h A} = \frac{1}{100 \times 0.0018} \approx 5.6\ \text{K/W},\qquad \tau = R C = 34\ \text{s}$$

**Burst response:**

$$\Delta T_{board}(t) = P R_{conv}\left(1-e^{-t/\tau}\right)$$

The steady-state asymptote is 79 × 5.6 ≈ 440 K, which is not survivable. In early time the board heats at ≈ 13 K/s.
